sections.bio:
Operator-turned-investor helping early-stage healthcare and consumer founders go from zero to one - VC scout for US/EU funds, Shark Tank India evaluator, 2x founder.

With 25+ years across global brands (Sanofi, GSK, Medela) and disruptive startups, I bring a unique intersection of corporate rigour and founder agility. From building Medela India from scratch to advising 2000+ ventures via Shark Tank India, I’ve led businesses across zero-to-one and scale-up phases focusing on category creation, P&L ownership, and GTM innovation.

🔹 Founded HealthArk – a B2B medtech trading firm representing global brands
🔹 Country Director – Medela: Built ₹50Cr+ breast pump business in India from ground up
🔹 Strategy & investment evaluator – Shark Tank India (Seasons 2, 3 & 4)
🔹 Mentor & advisor to early-stage founders on fundraising, market entry, and growth strategy
🔹 Angel investor with deep interest in eldercare, femtech, and digital health
🔹 Ex-officio at IIHMR University – bridging industry and academia
🔹Venture Scout with several US funds - supporting fund raising for early stage startups

I thrive at the confluence of mission-driven ventures, capital allocation, and high-trust relationships
Let’s connect if you’re building in health, wellness, or emerging India.

🌐 [www.amitrajgogia.com] | 📩 [[email protected]]

posts.text:
If your parents live in another city (in India) while you're working far away; would you pay for a medication reminder & monitoring service?

Here's how it works:
 📲 WhatsApp + Voice AI reminders in your parents' own language
 👩‍⚕️ Monitored by a human care team + clinical experts (not just an app)
 🔔 You get updates so you're not calling 3x a day to check "did you take your medicine & daily walk?"

Would you pay for this? If yes, how much/month would feel fair for peace of mind, not just a reminder app?

💬 Comment your number (or "wouldn't pay" ~ that's useful data too!)

Tag someone who worries about this daily, TIA 🙂

"Strategic clarity beats tools"

BCG found that employees with "strong strategic clarity and limited access to tools" outperformed (by 20 percentage points) those with "limited strategic clarity and strong access to tools."

source~Marketoonist Tom Fishburne 👏

sunday thoughts on crazy business models around us 😄 

👉 Monetising restaurant visibility by Zomato/Swiggy ads (charge commission, then charge again to be seen among others paying the same commission)
👉 Monetising driver earnings by Ola/Uber subscriptions (upfront daily fee, even before a ride is earned)
👉 Monetising queue-avoidance by IRCTC convenience fee (a government platform charging you to skip its own queue)
👉 Monetising financial hardship by credit card late fees (highest cost falls on those least able to pay on time)
👉 Monetising unemployment by Naukri priority listings (charging jobless users to be seen by recruiters browsing free)
👉 Monetising uncertainty by Astrotalk (per-minute billing on career, money, marriage anxiety)
👉 Monetising scarcity by UPSC coaching apps (the fewer the government jobs, the higher the willingness to pay)
👉 Monetising social pressure by matrimony sites (urgency to marry off kids = premium pricing power)
👉 Monetising merchants twice by PhonePe/GPay (free for users, MDR from merchants, then loans sold to the same merchants)
👉 Monetising non-claims by insurance aggregators (commission on the sale, insurer profits again every year you don't claim)
👉 Monetising leads twice by real estate portals (developers pay to list, then pay again to buy back their own buyer leads)
👉 Monetising lateness by traffic challan apps (fee for paying late, fee again for paying "conveniently")
👉 Monetising your attention by telecom zero-rating (brands pay telecoms to make data "free" for you)
👉 Monetising good behaviour by Cred (pays you to pay bills on time, sells that audience to brands)

i think award should go to LinkedIn for monetising unemployment via premium services 😮‍💨
